topic.name: Estimating Derivatives Using a Central Difference Quotient

question.text:
An oil tank is leaking $q(t)$ liters of oil after $t$ hours. The graph of $q(t)$ is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the oil is leaking from the tank when $t=2$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
question.explanation:
We use the central difference approximation \[ q'(t) \approx \frac{q(t+h) - q(t-h)}{2h}, \] at the time $t=2$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

\begin{align*} q'(2) &\approx \frac{q(2+1) - q(2-1)}{2}\\[5pt] &=\frac{q(3) - q(1)}{2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3-2}{2}\\[5pt] &=0.5. \end{align*}

Therefore, the rate of leaking at the instant of time $t = 2$ is $0.5\,\textrm{liters}/ \textrm{hour}.$

example.title: Estimating a Derivative Given a Graph Using a Central Difference Approximation: Word Problem

question.text:
A car travels on a straight road in such a way that its position, in meters, after $t$ seconds is given by the function $f(t).$ The values of $f(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

$t$ $2$ $4$ $6$ $8$ $10$ $12$
$f(t)$ $1$ $2$ $4$ $6$ $14$ $15$
\[\]

Approximate the velocity $f'(t)$ at the point $t = 4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h = 2.$
question.explanation:
We use the central difference approximation \[ f'(t) \approx \frac{f(t+h) - f(t-h)}{2h}, \] at the time $t=4$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives \begin{align*} f'(4) &\approx \frac{f(4+2) - f(4-2)}{2(2)}\\[5pt] &=\frac{f(6) - f(2)}{4}\\[5pt] &=\frac{4- 1}{4}\\[5pt] &=\frac{3}{4}\\[5pt] &=0.75. \end{align*}

Therefore, the velocity of the car at the instant of time $t = 4$ is $0.75\,\textrm{m}/\textrm{s}.$

example.title: Estimating a Derivative Given a Graph Using a Central Difference Approximation: Word Problem

question.text: The graph of the function $y = f(x)$ is shown above. Approximate $f'(x)$ at the point $x=4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
question.explanation:
We use the central difference approximation \[ f'(x) \approx \frac{f(x+h) - f(x-h)}{2h}, \] at the point $x=4$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

\begin{align*} f'(4) &\approx \frac{f(4+1) - f(4-1)}{2(1)}\\[5pt] &=\frac{f(5) - f(3)}{2}\\[5pt] &=\frac{4-0}{2}\\[5pt] &=\frac{4}{2}\\[5pt] &=2. \end{align*}
